about: The priest bows low, lays his joined hands on the altar and asks that an angel carry the offering to the altar on high. The angel is not named, and the tradition has never settled who he is: some saw Michael, some Christ himself, some refused to name him at all. Sublíme altáre — the altar on high — comes from Revelation 8. The sentence has one main verb (repleámur) with a conditional clause about those who will communicate wedged into the middle of it.

s01.narrative: The priest bows low and lays his joined hands upon the altar.

s02.translation: Humbly we beseech thee, almighty God: bid these things be carried by the hands of thy holy Angel to thine altar on high, into the sight of thy divine majesty:

s04.translation: that as many of us as, by partaking of this altar, shall receive the most holy

s05.narrative: The priest joins his hands and signs the cross once over the host and once over the chalice.

s06.translation: Body and Blood of thy Son,

s08.translation: may be filled with every heavenly blessing and grace.

s10.translation: Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

w001.function: An adjective, not an adverb: from sub and plicáre, to bend down under — it describes the posture the rubric has just commanded.

w007.function: An accusative neuter plural: the subject of the infinitive “perférri” (w008).

w008.function: The passive infinitive of a compound of fero, which is irregular and belongs to no conjugation.

w012.function: Singular: one angel, unnamed. The tradition has never settled who he is.

w023.function: The comma after ut sets off the whole clause about those who communicate, which is wedged between the conjunction and its verb “repleámur” (w041).

w024.function: Indeclinable: the form marks neither case nor gender nor number. The nominative plural follows from its being the subject of “sumpsérimus” (w035); no gender is claimed, because nothing marks one.

w028.function: From pártem cápere, to take a part; not presence but a share received.

w029.function: A Roman legal term: a sacrosánctus person could not be harmed without incurring a curse.

w035.function: A future perfect: the receiving is to be complete before the petition for grace is fulfilled. The form can also be a perfect subjunctive, but the conditional clause decides.

w040.function: An ablative with “repleámur” (w041): that with which one is filled.
